title: Roll out the rename beyond the site: domain, newsletter, email, partners
description:
The site is live as Conscious Communities but the rest of the world still says Developmental Spaces. Do these, in roughly this order. Reasoning and rules of use are in docs/branding/naming.md (section "Rules of use" and "Open items").

1. Domain: consciouscommunities.net is Rufus's (registered on Cloudflare 2026-01-03). Point it at developmentalspaces.org with a 301 redirect (Cloudflare redirect rule). consciouscommunities.org is parked for sale on Afternic and .com is taken; buying the .org is a Rufus decision, not assumed. consciouscollectives.org is also Rufus's and stays unused ("communities" is the better word). Keep developmentalspaces.org as the canonical domain; do not move it.
2. Newsletter: Substack (developmentalspaces.substack.com) display name to Conscious Communities; the URL stays. Check the About/description text there.
3. Email: the mailer repo (../devspaces-mailer, github life-itself/devspaces-mailer) still says "Developmental Spaces" in the subscribe confirmation page (src/index.js, link text, old cream palette #faf6ec / #2a2118) and in every email footer ("Developmental Spaces · Life Itself"). Change the visible name and restyle the confirmation page to the new look (near-white, ink, yellow, PT Serif). Do NOT change the sending address courses@mail.developmentalspaces.org or the DNS; the deliverability stack (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, plain-text part) was hard-won and works.
4. Partners: send a short note to Fetzer, Commonweal, Ekskaret, Springboard and LIONE that the public name is now Conscious Communities and why (two paragraphs from naming.md are enough). Ask Life Itself to update links and descriptions that say "Developmental Spaces initiative" (lifeitself.org posts such as building-field-for-developmental-spaces; the Life Itself site's own pages about this project).
5. Small places: GitHub repo description (currently "Manifesto website for developmental spaces and conscious coliving in an age between worlds."), Google Analytics property name (G-CN5D9D57PC), any social handles, email signature lines.
6. Social/OG: add an Open Graph image and check page titles and descriptions for the main pages (a card built from the road painting and the yellow block would do). Confirm the favicon shows in tabs.

Acceptance: searching the web and following old links lands people on a consistent Conscious Communities presence; nothing user-facing says only "Developmental Spaces" where it should say the public name, except the concept, paper, manifesto and network. The July blog post (blog/a-new-home-for-developmental-spaces.md) stays as a historical record.

title: Redesign follow-ups (Conscious Communities, direction E)
description:
Follow-up work after the Conscious Communities rename and the direction E (watercolour) redesign went live on 2026-09-19 (merge 2f80f16 on main; changelog entry changelog/2026-09-19-conscious-communities-redesign.md). Start a new session by reading AGENTS.md, then docs/branding/README.md (current state, links, decision log), then docs/branding/design-direction.md section 7 (the design rules in force).

STATE. Live in production: home, Learn, Build, Fund, Find, About, whitepaper and manifesto openers, the painted catalogue at the top of /what, restyled course signup forms. Site name is Conscious Communities; Developmental Spaces stays the name of the concept, whitepaper, manifesto and network (docs/branding/naming.md). Design: near-white page, PT Serif set tight, Source Sans 3, one yellow (#FFD23F), watercolour illustration, no photographs on the front door. All paintings are STAND-INS borrowed from the Awami Conscious Food book. The spiral mark is generated in code.

DECIDED (do not relitigate without Rufus): direction E over A to D; no photography commission; the site is about the general idea, not the Bergerac hub; illustration carries ideas and photographs only appear as captioned documentary plates on pages about actual places; Samarra etching is good but belongs inside as a plate, not on a cover; copy is a separate human job; naming decision is not to be revisited until six months after go-live (see the deferred review bead).

SUGGESTED ORDER. 1) rename rollout and announcement (the site is already live under the new name, so the rest of the world is now inconsistent); 2) copy pass (Rufus writes, Claude edits); 3) /what rebuild; 4) remaining interior pages; 5) QA pass; 6) illustrations, then whitepaper cover and diagram, which depend on them; 7) housekeeping.

WORKING NOTES. Preview with `fl . --yes` (site ds-redesign-preview). The preview skips the build/ folder, lags on custom.css by 10 to 20 minutes, and ignores contentExclude; AGENTS.md has the workarounds. Pushing to main deploys to production within about a minute. docs/ is excluded from the site but visible on the public GitHub repo. The two Claude artifacts (mood board, home mockups) are linked in docs/branding/README.md with their source saved in docs/branding/moodboard-artifact/ and docs/branding/mockups/.

title: Rebuild /what as a designed catalogue page aligned with the whitepaper
description: Currently a normal Flowershow markdown page with the catalogue grid bolted on top. Rebuild as layout: plain in the catalogue style (mockup 3, docs/branding/mockups/), with content restructured to follow the paper's executive summary: definition, five domains (paper nomenclature: waking up, cognitive, growing up, cleaning up, showing up), why dedicated spaces (containment, community, continuity), characteristics. Old outline material moves to an appendix or the wiki.

title: Migrate ratified consolidation decisions and analysis into internal docs
description:
Create a durable, source-attributed internal record in this repository of the decisions and analysis already completed in the sibling checkout `../devspaces-consolidation`.

Scope: start from its ratified/decision-bearing material, especially `BRIEF.md`, `brand-narrative.md`, `motivation.md`, `sitemap.md`, `PLAN.md`, and relevant `ref/` records. Preserve the reasoning and provenance behind choices about the Developmental Spaces brand and naming, mission/positioning, audience hierarchy, job stories, information architecture, voice/register, and any explicitly locked decisions.

Do not treat every historical draft as current policy. Separate ratified/locked choices from open questions and working proposals. Cross-link or summarize primary source files where copying them verbatim would create needless divergence.

Prerequisite: the top-level `docs/` directory must be excluded from Flower Show publication.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/` contains a clear, discoverable decision/strategy record for this project.
- It captures at minimum: the Developmental Spaces umbrella name and public-language doctrine; ratified tagline and its status; mission/positioning; primary and secondary audiences; Learn/Build/Fund job stories and IA; voice/register; and any relevant brand design direction.
- Each entry identifies its source file and decision date/status, and distinguishes locked decisions from open items.
- Relevant reasoning/analysis is retained or linked so future contributors can understand why choices were made.
- A review compares the inventory against `../devspaces-consolidation` and records intentional omissions.

title: Exclude internal docs from Flower Show publishing
description:
Configure this repository so the top-level `docs/` directory is excluded from Flower Show’s published content while remaining tracked in Git.

Context: the repository needs a private-to-the-site documentation area for strategy, decisions, and implementation notes. Flower Show should not generate routes or navigation entries from files under `docs/`.

Implementation notes:
- Identify and use Flower Show’s supported ignore/exclusion mechanism (rather than relying only on navigation omission).
- Keep existing publishable Markdown content outside `docs/` unaffected.
- Document the convention briefly so future internal documentation is placed under `docs/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- A representative Markdown file under `docs/` produces no published Flower Show page.
- Existing public pages continue to build and publish normally.
- The exclusion is committed as repository configuration and the `docs/` convention is documented.
close_reason: Done 2026-09-19: contentExclude now lists /docs, /.beads, /sandbox, /README, /AGENTS, /CLAUDE in config.json. Verified in production: /docs, /docs/branding, /.beads, /sandbox all return 404.
